spec.title: Steward tree

p.TREE-SKILL-SCOPE: Render the plan a human can already read; change nothing. The viewer is derived navigation under [plan-hierarchy.xml#TREE-VIEWER-IS-DERIVED](../../flows/multi-user-planning/plan-hierarchy.xml), never a second plan, a queue or an authority. It grants no execution or acceptance authority and is not a status report: a central session still owes the ordinary verified status, and a worker uses only its packet's named inputs.

p.TREE-SKILL-GENERIC: The renderer is plan-shaped, not project-shaped: no project ids, layers, tabs or inventories. Any conformant plan renders — the node tree by `order`, the protocol's full state vocabulary, kinds, both dependency kinds, mandates, acceptance and evidence. Unrecognised per-node or plan-level fields are shown generically in the detail pane instead of being special-cased or dropped.

p.TREE-SKILL-EDGES: Dependencies are typed edges, shown in both directions and named by kind, never merged: `depends_on` reads as the inherited start gate («Предпосылка старта») and `completes_after` as this node's own completion gate («Завершается после»), per [plan-hierarchy.xml#COMPLETION-GATES](../../flows/multi-user-planning/plan-hierarchy.xml). A kind a plan does not use takes no space in the pane.

p.TREE-SKILL-RUN: Run the packaged Python 3.11+ renderer on a steward context. `--resolve`, run inside the checkout, finds the context through `steward-common`; `--context` names it directly. Either reads `<context>/plan.toml` and writes `<context>/view/` unless `--out` names another directory. `--plan` with `--out` still renders any plan file. Nothing outside the output directory is written and the plan is opened read-only:

spec.fence: python -B scripts/render_tree.py --resolve [--home <steward home>] [--lang ru|en] [--watch] python -B scripts/render_tree.py --context <steward home>/contexts/<context-id> [--out <directory>] python -B scripts/render_tree.py --plan <plan.toml> --out <directory> [--lang ru|en] [--watch]

p.TREE-SKILL-VIEW-DISPOSABLE: The context's `view/` is a disposable projection: delete it at any time, regenerate it from the plan, never read it back. It embeds no absolute path, so a copied steward home carries no stale machine path. Nothing outside the steward home is a planning source of truth.

p.TREE-SKILL-LAUNCHER: `bin/plan-tree` is a convenience command for people: run in any checkout of a project that installs this package, it re-renders the view through `--resolve` and prints the path of `index.html`; `--open` also shows it in the default browser, `--repo` names another checkout and `--lang` picks the language. It finds the newest installed copy of this package inside the checkout, needs Git on PATH, runs itself on Python 3.8 or newer and starts the renderer with Python 3.11 or newer, saying so when none is installed. To use it, copy the files of `bin/` into a directory on PATH; on macOS and Linux make `plan-tree` executable, on Windows `plan-tree.ps1` and `plan-tree.cmd` run the same launcher from PowerShell and cmd. It writes nothing but the view.

p.TREE-SKILL-OUTPUT: The output directory receives `index.html`, a self-contained offline page with no network, font or script dependency, and `plan-tree.json`, the same model for other readers. Both are replaced atomically and only when their bytes change, so a reload never sees a half-written page and an unchanged plan re-renders byte-identically. `--watch` re-renders on changed plan bytes at `--interval` seconds. Output carries no timestamp: the plan's own `updated_at`, `revision` and sha256 identify what was rendered.

p.TREE-SKILL-VOCABULARY: States are displayed through the buckets fixed by `plan-hierarchy.xml#TREE-DISPLAY-BUCKETS`, with `candidate` («Сделано · ждёт приёмки») named distinctly from `accepted` («Готово · принято»), and `dropped` / `superseded` as «Закрыто без выполнения». Per-parent counts follow `#TREE-LEAF-COUNTING` — leaf descendants only, each leaf once, so a parent's buckets sum to its leaf total. Counts are not progress and not acceptance.

p.TREE-SKILL-VALIDATION: The page always shows the verdict of the package's own validator (`steward-parallel/scripts/parallel_frontier.py`, which runs the goal renderer's structural checks first), so the picture cannot contradict the tools. An invalid or unparsable plan still renders its nodes under a refusal banner naming the code and message. Unknown states, orphans, parent cycles and dangling dependency targets appear as per-node warnings; the viewer never invents a readiness for them.

p.TREE-SKILL-UI: One page, no build step: search by id or title, expand and collapse, a jump to `current_node`, light/dark/auto theme, a Russian/English string table selectable in the page, keyboard navigation over an ARIA tree, and a layout that works at phone width. The tree uses the full document width with no permanent reserved detail column. Details open in a separate closable fixed right panel, never inserted into the tree; on desktop only while open, the tree uses all remaining space to its left so badges are not obscured. Mobile uses an overlay. Every task stays one nowrap row, titles ellipsize with full tooltip/details and compact numeric status badges remain right-aligned. Escape closes the panel and restores focus to its node. Compact right-aligned colored count badges use the payload's leaf-descendant buckets, with accessible status/count labels, not a recomputed history or progress. Document scrolling, offline file access and mobile-width overlay remain supported. The keyboard-accessible All / Unfinished / In progress control defaults to All. Unfinished excludes only accepted/dropped/superseded (candidate, blocked and deferred remain); In progress matches the node's own active state. Search intersects that filter. Only matches and their ancestor context appear, with matching branches initially expanded and unrelated siblings omitted. Filtered branches can then be collapsed/reopened by twisty or ArrowLeft/ArrowRight; reopening reveals only matching descendant/context rows. This filtered expansion is separate, so All restores ordinary expansion. Search has the same collapsible behavior. Counts always describe the full payload branch, not the filtered subset. A node id in the URL fragment opens that node, so a review can point at one node instead of describing where to click. Plan text is data and never markup: titles, acceptance and evidence are injected as text, so a plan cannot script the page.

p.TREE-SKILL-REPORT: Report the output path, plan id, revision, sha256, node count, the validator verdict and the warning count; name the buckets a reviewer should look at rather than restating the whole tree. A rendered view is evidence about the plan's shape, never acceptance of its nodes. Select economical checks under [verification-selection.xml](../../flows/multi-user-planning/verification-selection.xml); judge candidates with [collaboration-and-acceptance.xml](../../flows/multi-user-planning/collaboration-and-acceptance.xml).
